sections.h2: Where is Charleston, West Virginia, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Charleston is the state capital and its largest city, set on the Kanawha River where the Elk River joins it. It is the seat of Kanawha County, and its elevation runs from 597 to 1,167 feet. The city covers 32.5 square miles, of which 31.4 are land.

Fifteen named neighborhoods sit inside the city limits, from the East End and Edgewood historic districts to the West Side, South Hills, Kanawha City, Elk City, Fort Hill, Forest Hills and North Charleston. Others include Charleston Heights, Louden Heights, Riverview, Shadowlawn, South Park and South Ruffner. Flood exposure and house age vary by neighborhood, so name the neighborhood when you ask the city about an address.

sections.h2: How did Charleston's history shape its housing?
sections.html:
Settlers built Fort Lee by the Kanawha in April 1788, and Virginia designated 40 acres of George Clendenin's land as a town in December 1794. Salt was the first big industry, with the first furnace built in 1797, and salt works eventually lined the south bank in what is now Kanawha City.

The capital moved to Charleston in 1870, went back to Wheeling in 1875 and returned permanently in 1885. The Chesapeake and Ohio arrived in 1873, and between 1880 and 1930 the population rose from 4,192 to 60,408. A fire destroyed the Victorian capitol in January 1921, and the present building, designed by Cass Gilbert, was dedicated in 1932.

Urban renewal in the 1960s demolished many buildings, especially in the Triangle District. The encyclopedia says that after the demolition it took years for those areas to recover and that a number of vacant lots from that period still exist. Since the 1960 peak the city has lost population, which the encyclopedia ties to declining chemical industry jobs and out-migration.

sections.h2: What does the Charleston economy run on?
sections.html:
Government and health care anchor it, and the chemical industry is far smaller than it was. The Charleston Area Medical Center, created in 1972 by merging the major hospitals, serves southern West Virginia and is among the state's largest employers.

  • State government is based at the Capitol complex, and the Culture Center there houses the state archives and museum.
  • The Charleston area is home to Appalachian Power, United Bank and Gestamp, according to Wikipedia's list of companies headquartered there.
  • The University of Charleston, founded as Morris Harvey College, has about 1,000 students, and a West Virginia University branch campus serves as a clinical campus.
  • The Clay Center for the Arts and Sciences, the Vandalia Health Center civic center and the FestivALL events bring visitors.

The city's Municipal Auditorium, a 1939 art moderne landmark, closed in 2024 over structural and safety concerns.

sections.h2: What are Charleston's climate and flood risks?
sections.html:
Charleston has a humid subtropical climate with four seasons, and flooding is the hazard that most affects a house sale. The January daily average is 34.4 degrees Fahrenheit, the city sees about 23 days a year at 90 or above, and precipitation averages about 3.5 inches a month. Thunderstorms are frequent in late spring and summer and are occasionally severe.

The city's own floodplain page says Charleston has had 13 floods greater than the 1 percent annual chance flood, the last in 1934, and that damage has occurred in smaller events too. The Floodplain Manager reviews building permits and will determine whether a property is in a Special Flood Hazard Area, where flood insurance is typically required. An Elevation Certificate from a licensed surveyor or engineer can help set premiums and can support a map amendment request.

sections.h2: How do roads, transit and schools affect a Charleston sale?
sections.html:
Charleston is crossed by Interstates 64, 77 and 79, and the West Virginia Turnpike ends at the city's southeastern edge. U.S. 60 and U.S. 119 run through the center, and West Virginia routes 25, 61, 62 and 114 lie within the limits. Yeager Airport is about two miles north of the interstates on route 114, and Amtrak's Cardinal stops in the city. The Kanawha Valley Regional Transportation Authority runs the buses.

Public schools belong to Kanawha County Schools. The city's high schools are Capital High School, George Washington High School in South Hills and the private Charleston Catholic High School. Confirm the school assignment for a specific address with the district.

sections.h2: What permits and repairs matter before selling a Charleston house?
sections.html:
All construction work in Charleston needs a permit before it begins, and the Building Department says homeowners may do their own work if permits are pulled and an inspection confirms the work meets code. The department issues permits for roofs, replacement windows, siding, fences, retaining walls, driveways, plumbing, electrical and HVAC, among other work.

  • Permit fees are waived for construction with a total job cost up to $2,500.
  • Contractors who start without a permit face a minimum $100 fee or twice the normal fee, whichever is greater, and a license suspension of at least three months.
  • Demolition permits require an asbestos report and details on capping the storm and sewer laterals.
  • Applications go to the Permit Coordinator, Building Department, 915 Quarrier Street, Suite 5, and the permit office number is 304-348-6833.

The permit rules apply to repairs made before a sale, and a buyer's inspection can raise questions about unpermitted work.

sections.h2: Who collects and who assesses property tax on a Charleston home?
sections.html:
Kanawha County, not the city, bills property tax. The Kanawha County Sheriff's Tax Division collects it, and the Kanawha County Assessor values the property.

The tax office also runs detachments in Cross Lanes, Sissonville, Elkview, Jefferson and Quincy, and its page says it mails roughly 100,000 real estate tickets and 95,000 personal property tickets each July. The statewide calendar applies: tickets on or after July 15, installments due September 1 and March 1, a 2.5 percent discount before each date, delinquency on October 1 and April 1, and 9 percent annual interest on late tax. Property inside a municipality that is not an owner-occupied home is Class IV, which the state taxes at four times the Class I rate, while owner-occupied residential property is Class II at two times.

sections.h2: What do closing costs look like on a Charleston sale?
sections.html:
The main government charge is the transfer tax recorded with the deed. West Virginia Code 11-22-2 sets $1.10 per $500 of value, kept by the county since July 1, 2025, plus an additional county tax of 55 cents per $500 unless the commission has raised it, plus a $20 fee on transfers for consideration.

On a $150,000 deed at those base rates the amounts are $330, $165 and $20, a total of $515. The grantor pays unless the grantee accepts the deed with the tax unpaid. Unpaid property tax, prior mortgages and any liens come out of the proceeds, so ask the sheriff's office for the tax status before you accept any number.

sections.h2: What do Charleston sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Three situations are worth planning for: older houses, properties near the rivers and inherited homes. The East End and Edgewood carry historic district designations, and homes near the Kanawha and Elk rivers raise the flood questions covered above.

A list, a sale by owner or a cash sale each handles those issues differently. A listing brings showings and buyer financing, and a cash sale usually involves a title search, payoff of any liens, and a deed recorded with the county. Compare what each leaves you after taxes, liens and transfer costs, not the headline price alone.

faqs.q: Does the City of Charleston or Kanawha County collect property tax?
faqs.a: Kanawha County does. The Sheriff's Tax Division at 409 Virginia Street East collects it, and the phone number is 304-357-0210.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a roof or window replacement in Charleston?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's Building Department lists roofs and replacement windows among the work that needs a permit, and fees are waived only when the total job cost is $2,500 or less.

faqs.q: How do I find out if a Charleston house is in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Ask the city's Floodplain Manager for a floodplain determination, or check the state's flood hazard tool. A property in a Special Flood Hazard Area typically needs flood insurance, and an Elevation Certificate can help with premiums.

faqs.q: What transfer tax applies when I sell a Charleston house?
faqs.a: The base rates are $1.10 per $500 of value plus an additional county tax of 55 cents per $500, plus a $20 fee, unless the Kanawha County Commission has raised its rate. The seller pays unless the buyer accepts the deed with the tax unpaid.

faqs.q: When are Kanawha County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Installments are due September 1 and March 1, with a 2.5 percent discount for paying before each date. Unpaid halves become delinquent on October 1 and April 1 and accrue 9 percent interest.
